title: Edsger W. Dijkstra
name: Edsger W. Dijkstra
summary: Dutch computer scientist whose work on algorithms, structured programming, and disciplined reasoning transformed software engineering and theoretical computer science.
whyThisMatters: Dijkstra argued that programs should be reasoned about with rigor, a principle that underlies modern work on reliable and secure software. His shortest-path algorithm and work on concurrency remain staples of computing.

sections.overview:
Edsger W. Dijkstra was a Dutch computer scientist whose work on algorithms, programming methodology, and concurrency helped define modern computer science. His shortest-path algorithm remains a basic tool in networks and graph processing.

Discipline in programming

Dijkstra championed structured programming and precise reasoning about programs. His emphasis on clarity and correctness has direct relevance to secure systems, which must resist both design errors and implementation mistakes.

In memoriam

Dijkstra died in 2002. His writing and technical work continue to challenge engineers to treat programming as a discipline of careful thought.

timeline.event: Develops the shortest-path algorithm while working at the Mathematical Centre in Amsterdam.
Completes a PhD at the University of Amsterdam.
Receives the ACM A.M. Turing Award.
